steps.text: Some materials let electricity flow through them. Let's test which ones complete the circuit and light the bulb.
Pick a metal first — tap Copper.
Now tap “Test” to place it in the circuit.
The bulb lights up — metals have free electrons that carry current, so they're good conductors.
Now test a non-metal — the bulb stays off. Metals conduct electricity, most non-metals do not.

coach.mission: Test a metal and a non-metal in the circuit and see which lights the bulb.
whenStuck: Tap a material first, then tap “Test”.
Try a metal like Copper, then a non-metal, and compare.
whenWrong: Metals light the bulb (conductors); non-metals leave it off.
If the bulb stayed off, that material is a non-metal — not a conductor.
whenCorrect: Right — the metal completed the circuit, so it conducts electricity.
Good — the non-metal didn't conduct, so the bulb stayed off.
coach.done: You've seen that metals conduct electricity and most non-metals don't. Test more, or move on when you're ready.
